user.current_work: Social media manager at a local agency

user_snapshot: Two years post-NYSC, grinding as an agency social media manager in Yaba on ₦150k with ₦450k saved, ₦30k monthly family load, and a committed JAPA plan inside 18 months.
headline_insight: Your current ₦150k agency role is undervaluing skills (SMM + video + writing) that pay $1.5-4k/mo remote — which means your JAPA runway should be USD-funded, not naira-funded. Stop saving in naira; start earning in USD within 6 months.

routes.title: Remote Content Marketing / Social Manager (USD clients)
routes.one_liner: Replace your ₦150k agency salary with $1.5-3k/mo remote retainers, then fund JAPA from USD earnings.

fit_reasons.note: Your SMM + content + video editing + writing stack is exactly what US/UK SaaS brands pay retainers for.
Committed 18-month JAPA plan needs USD income; naira ₦150k cannot fund ₦8-15m Canada or UK routes.

break_reasons.risk: Cold-pitching without a niche portfolio stalls at $0 for 4-6 months; agency work doesn't auto-translate to client work.

routes.who_this_fits: Agency creatives who can self-direct, pitch cold, and package existing work into a niche portfolio site.
routes.who_this_breaks: People who wait for job posts instead of DMing founders and treating Twitter/LinkedIn as distribution.

real_cost.what_you_give_up: Evenings and weekends for 6 months building portfolio + outbound, while keeping the ₦150k agency job as base.

real_pay.range_note: USD-pegged: $600 entry / $1.6k mid / $3.5k+ senior monthly retainers. Converted at ₦1,500/$.

routes.two_year_projection: In 2 years, if you niche into B2B SaaS or creator-economy content, you're on $2.5-3.5k/mo (₦3.7-5.2m) retainers, landed in Toronto on a study permit or UK Graduate visa, funded from your own USD savings.
pro_tips: Niche down: pick B2B SaaS, fintech, or creator tools — not 'social media' broadly.
Pitch founders on Twitter/LinkedIn directly, not job boards; reply rate is 10x higher.

routes.nigerian_notes: Open a Geegpay, Grey, or Payoneer USD account NOW — don't wait for first client. Domiciliary naira conversion eats 2-4% if you route through local banks.

routes.title: UK MSc (Digital Marketing / Media) → Graduate Visa → Skilled Worker
routes.one_liner: 1-year taught MSc in the UK, then 2-year post-study work visa, route into an agency or in-house marketing role.

fit_reasons.note: Committed 18-month horizon fits UK September intake perfectly — apply now for Sept 2026.
Mass Comm 2:1 from a private university meets UK MSc entry bar without a GRE or bridging year.

break_reasons.risk: ₦450k savings covers nothing — you need ₦18-25m total; funding gap must come from family, loan, or USD income route above.

routes.who_this_fits: Grads who can raise ₦20m via family, LAPO/AELEX loan, or 12 months of USD freelance stacking.
routes.who_this_breaks: Anyone assuming Leverage Edu or an agent will 'sort the funds' — proof-of-funds is real and audited.

real_cost.what_you_give_up: ₦22m+ in tuition and living costs, plus one year of Nigerian income while studying full-time.

real_pay.range_note: UK post-study: £28-35k entry / £45-55k mid / £70k+ senior annually. Converted at ₦1,850/£.

routes.two_year_projection: In 2 years, if you land Sept 2026 intake, you graduate mid-2027 on a Graduate visa, working a £32-38k junior marketing role in Manchester or Birmingham (cheaper than London), earning ~₦5m/mo equivalent.
pro_tips: Target Russell Group unis with scholarships: Sheffield, Leeds, Cardiff — avoid pay-to-enrol London commuter schools.
Apply January-March for September; late applicants lose CAS and scholarship windows.

routes.nigerian_notes: Don't use unregistered agents; use the university's direct application portal. Proof-of-funds must sit in a CBN-approved bank for 28 days before CAS — plan liquidity accordingly.

routes.title: In-House Content / Social Lead at Nigerian Fintech
routes.one_liner: Move from agency grind to in-house content lead at Paystack, Moniepoint, Kuda, or PiggyVest — 3-4x your current pay.

fit_reasons.note: Agency SMM + video + writing is the exact stack fintech content teams hire for at the ₦450-700k level.
Yaba puts you 20 minutes from Paystack, Flutterwave, and Kuda offices for interviews and networking.

break_reasons.risk: Fintech content roles attract 400+ applicants; without a personal brand or referral you stay stuck in agency pay bands.

routes.who_this_fits: Agency creatives who can show B2C metrics (growth, conversion, viral posts) and have a warm referral in.
routes.who_this_breaks: People who apply cold via Jobberman without building inbound through Twitter/LinkedIn first.

real_cost.what_you_give_up: 3 months of intense outbound + portfolio rebuild while holding current agency role.

real_pay.range_note: Tier-1 fintech (Paystack, Moniepoint) pays top of range; tier-2 (Kuda, PiggyVest, Cowrywise) pays ₦400-700k entry.

routes.two_year_projection: In 2 years, if you land a fintech content role, you're Senior Content Manager at Moniepoint or Cowrywise on ₦1-1.5m/mo, with ₦8-12m saved — which makes the UK MSc or Canada PR route actually fundable.
pro_tips: DM the current content lead, not HR — ask for a 15-min coffee, not a job.
Build one Twitter thread per week breaking down a Nigerian fintech's marketing — tag them.

routes.title: Build a Niche Content Brand (YouTube/TikTok/Newsletter)
routes.one_liner: Build a niche content asset in a high-CPM topic (money, tech, career) that pays ad + sponsor revenue in USD.

fit_reasons.note: Video editing + writing + SMM is the exact three-stack needed to run a one-person creator business.
High risk tolerance and low family pressure means you can invest 12 months with minimal revenue.

break_reasons.risk: Monetisation typically starts month 9-14; most Nigerian creators quit at month 4 when income is still ₦0.

routes.who_this_fits: Obsessive creators who can publish 2-3x weekly for 12 months before seeing meaningful revenue.
routes.who_this_breaks: Anyone who needs validation (views, likes) to keep posting, or treats it as a side-side hustle.

real_cost.what_you_give_up: 10-15 hours weekly for 12 months with near-zero revenue until month 9; social life compressed.

real_pay.range_note: YouTube AdSense + sponsors, USD-pegged. Top Nigerian creators in tech/money hit $4-8k/mo by year 2-3.

routes.two_year_projection: In 2 years, if you ship consistently in one niche, you have 30-80k subscribers, $1-2.5k/mo (₦1.5-3.7m) in AdSense + sponsors, and a portable brand you take to Canada or the UK.
pro_tips: Pick one platform and one niche — don't cross-post to 4 platforms in month one.
High-CPM niches for Nigerians: personal finance, tech careers, JAPA — avoid lifestyle/vlog.
